findings.title: A backup code can be used without verifying the primary credential
findings.body: The new backup-code branch authenticates whenever a supplied backup code matches, but password verification above is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is non-empty (line 121), regardless of whether that TOTP value is valid. A caller can post an email, any dummy `totpCode`, and a valid backup code directly to the credentials callback and obtain a session without the password (and can similarly bypass the identity-provider checks guarded by `!credentials.totpCode`). The UI preserves the password during the normal two-step flow, but the server must enforce this invariant itself. Require a verified primary credential before accepting either TOTP or a backup code, or use a server-bound challenge indicating that the first step was completed.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing reuse under concurrent logins
findings.body: Each authorization request reads and decrypts the entire backup-code array, marks its matching entry as null locally, and then writes the full array back. Two concurrent requests using the same code can both read the original array, both validate it, and both successfully create sessions before either write occurs. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's consumption, restoring a code that another request already used. Consume the code with an atomic conditional database update/version check (or store individually hashed backup codes with a uniqueness/used-state condition) so only one request can claim a code.

findings.title: The added E2E coverage does not exercise backup-code authentication or consumption
findings.body: The test only checks that generated codes can be downloaded and copied; it never logs out and signs in with a backup code, checks an invalid code is rejected, or verifies that a successfully used code cannot be reused. Those are the feature's security-critical paths, including the new credentials-provider mutation logic, and the TODO explicitly acknowledges the omission. Add end-to-end or integration coverage for valid login, invalid login, single-use behavior, and backup-code-based 2FA disablement.
